items.s: She hoped to win the race, so finishing in fourth place was ____.
The train was so ____ that many people had to stand for the whole journey.
Only an ____ time can be accepted as a national record.
Swimming across a wide lake in one day would be an ____ achievement for anyone.
He is 41, but he is still ____ against much younger runners.

match.d: have no more of something left
move ahead of the group you were with
get back your strength after hard effort
so impressive that people notice and talk about it

items.s: On 11 October 2026, the Kenyan runner ____ the Melbourne Marathon.
In 2019, he ____ a marathon in under two hours.
Younger athletes often find it easier ____ their speed.
So far, Kipchoge ____ a long and successful career.
Kipchoge's win does not mean that age has stopped ____ him.

tfn.s: His 2019 sub-two-hour run counted as an official world record.
tfn.why: The text says it "did not count as an official world record because the conditions were different from a normal race."

tfn.s: Kipchoge's winning time in Melbourne was a record for the race.
tfn.why: The text says: "a new record for the race."

tfn.s: Kipchoge has said he will retire after this season.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say whether he plans to retire.

tfn.s: Some people taking part said the event was too crowded.
tfn.why: The text says: "Some ordinary participants complained that water stations ran out of drinks and that the event was overcrowded."

tfn.s: His Melbourne time was one of the fastest of his career.
tfn.why: The text says the win "was not one of the fastest times of his career."

pre.d: the work or sport that someone does for many years
the best result that anyone has ever had
a win
people who take part in something
something good that you did with a lot of effort
the habit of doing hard things every day
the most that someone can do
a large group of people in one place

focus.note: Some words go with one small word. Learn them together: proud of, worry about, depend on.

items.s: She is very proud ____ her son's medal.
Many runners worry ____ the weather before a race.
Many older people are interested ____ running a marathon.
A marathon runner depends ____ good training.
He is famous ____ his speed.
Runners must be over eighteen to be ____ to enter the race.
The online form was so ____ that it took me only two minutes to fill in.
The captain's ____ action in the last minute won the match for the team.
The documentary was so ____ that nobody in the room could look away.
The old bridge was damaged but still ____ after the storm; no part of it had fallen.
Winning every race in a season is an ____ target for most athletes.

match.d: move further ahead of the others
compensate for something that is missing
decide that someone or something cannot succeed
among the very best in a field

items.s: By the time the amateurs arrived, the champion ____ and gone home.
Many complaints ____ about the water supply after the race.
Runners ____ plenty of water before a long race.
Kipchoge ____ two Olympic marathon titles.
If the organisers had ordered more water, fewer runners ____.

tfn.s: Kipchoge has won the Olympic marathon more than once.
tfn.why: The text says: "He won Olympic marathon titles in Rio and Tokyo"

tfn.s: His Melbourne time was a personal best.
tfn.why: The text says: "His winning time was some way short of his personal best"

tfn.s: The organisers have apologised for the water shortages.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say whether the organisers apologised.

tfn.s: The 2019 Vienna run took place under the same conditions as an ordinary race.
tfn.why: The text says it "used special conditions, including rotating pacemakers."

tfn.s: The two Australian runners could not keep up with the winner.
tfn.why: The text says: "Australians Thomas Do Canto and Reece Edwards were unable to stay with him."

pre.d: people or teams you compete against
to stop working or playing a sport for good
the time it takes to feel strong again after effort
the parts of the body where bones meet, like the knee
people who do a sport for fun, not as a job
natural feelings that tell you what to do
strong wishes to achieve something
a strong force or strain on something

focus.note: Many verbs and adjectives need one fixed preposition. Learn the whole pair, such as cope with, rely on, specialise in.

items.s: Experience cannot always compensate ____ a loss of speed.
Some critics object ____ the idea that older athletes should retire.
Athletes have to cope ____ the pressure of competing at a high level.
He specialises ____ long-distance races.
Marathon training relies ____ patience and routine.
The invention of the carbon-plated shoe has ____ the way distance runners train.
His form has ____ wildly this season, with a brilliant win followed by a poor finish.
As the storm worsened, the crowds ____ the stadium and left the pitch empty.
The protest looked spontaneous, but it was in fact carefully ____ by the party's press team.
Her savings had ____ so much interest over ten years that she could retire.
The deadline was ____ by a week after complaints from applicants.

match.d: use experience or knowledge you already have
fail to notice or think about something
easily upset and needing careful handling

items.s: There was widespread ____ about whether the champion would ever race again.
The coach praised the squad's ____ in a season of unpredictable results.
Fame rarely brings ____ from criticism.
Spectators described the first-aid arrangements at the finish as woefully ____.
Only a handful of athletes sustain such ____ over two decades.

tfn.s: The writer implies that the amateur runners' difficulties deserve as much attention as the winner's result.
tfn.why: The text says a marathon's success "is also measured by what happens to the less celebrated people behind him."

tfn.s: The writer argues that the Melbourne win proves Kipchoge's decline has ended.
tfn.why: The text says "one result cannot erase the consequences of age."

tfn.s: Kipchoge's coach advised him to stay with the leading group in Melbourne.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text mentions no coach or instructions.

tfn.s: Kipchoge's Melbourne time was slower than his best marks.
tfn.why: The text says the win "did not require a return to his former, world-record-breaking pace."

tfn.s: Both the Vienna run and the Melbourne race took place under conditions allowed in ordinary competition.
tfn.why: The text says the Vienna "assistance and pacing arrangements differed from those permitted in ordinary competition."

how the body works
problems that stop you from making progress
hard physical effort

focus.note: At C1, learn fixed phrases as a block: tantamount to, contingent on, fraught with, wary of, exempt from.

items.s: Retiring now would be tantamount ____ admitting defeat.
The success of the event is contingent ____ the weather.
Any attempt to break the record is fraught ____ risk.
She was wary ____ announcing a retirement that she might regret.
Athletes are rarely exempt ____ the effects of ageing.

speak.title: Role-play: am I too old to race?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your friend is 45 and wants to run a marathon in six months. You think it's too hard on the body. Ask at least two questions, then say what you really think.

b.text: You're 45 and you want to run your first marathon. Explain why it matters to you and how you'll train safely. Try to get your friend's support.

phrases: I'm worried that it's too much for you.
I've always wanted to do it.
How are you going to train?
I'll start slowly and build up.
Age is just a number, isn't it?
I'll support you, but please be careful.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the friend agree to support the plan, and was that a good decision?
